title: Release v003: the load probe becomes opt-in instead of hardcoded
notes: The generated evaluator decided to be a rate probe purely from its own service name and environment: demo-orders in Production, always. Changing the declared traffic pattern had no effect, so s017 restarted the container and it simply kept probing.

A service name must never decide traffic shape on its own. The probe is now opt-in through DEMO_LOAD_PROBE, which Compose sets only for tuples whose declared pattern is paced. Configuration and behaviour finally agree.

Consequence: demo-orders Production evaluates all seven flags it owns, including demo-email-notifications-v2 and all three false-silence controls, instead of demo-cart-v2 alone. Under a two-evaluator budget that is the difference between a provable Production drain and an unprovable one.

Found by reading the running probe output rather than the configuration, which had looked correct throughout. Third defect in this family: flags[0] only, hardcoded cluster offsets, and now hardcoded probe selection.
